title: NOT EVEN A DOG WILL BARK

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"But among the Israelites not a dog will bark at any person or animal.' Then you
will know that the LORD makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel." -
Ex 11:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
What a picture. In Egypt, wailing that shakes the nation. In Goshen, such
stillness that not even a dog barks.

This is not a claim that Israel was better than Egypt. Exodus and Numbers make
it very clear that Israel grumbled, doubted, and rebelled repeatedly. The
difference was not their goodness. The difference was God's choice to redeem
them and, as chapter 12 will show, the blood on the doorpost.

The word "distinction" matters. God draws a line, and He is the one who draws
it. That is uncomfortable to modern ears, but it is honest to the text. What
makes anyone safe is not their record but their shelter.

For believers today, our peace does not come from being better than our
neighbours. It comes from being covered by Christ. "There is now no condemnation
for those who are in Christ Jesus" (Rom 8:1). The quietness in Goshen that night
was not the quiet of people who had earned safety. It was the quiet of people
who had trusted God's provision and gone indoors.

If your heart is restless tonight, the answer is not to try harder. It is to
rest where God has told you to rest.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you resting in Christ's work or in your own performance?
2. What would change if you truly believed there is no condemnation for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, I have nothing to offer but You. Thank You that in You there is no
condemnation. Give me the quietness of a heart that trusts. Amen.
